outcome: No event since 26 January 2024 settles the problem as stated; the in-window work is partial, variant, or conditional, and the largest new claim (OpenAI's September-October 2026 BSD-type manuscripts for Selmer corank 0 or 1) is unreviewed and I could not read its manuscript text.
problem_asks: Statement (Wikipedia, Jan 2024): 'determine precisely what rational numbers are congruent numbers', described as a corollary of the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture via Tunnell's theorem. Parts: (1) For each rational n > 0 (equivalently each positive squarefree integer n, since congruence is unchanged by multiplying by a rational square), decide whether n is the area of a right triangle with rational sides; equivalently whether E_n: y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x has a rational point with y not 0 (positive rank). (2) Give this determination 'precisely', i.e. a characterisation or test that decides every n. The statement does not say whether the determination must be unconditional; its parenthetical names Tunnell's criterion as the route, which is unconditional in the forward direction (congruent implies count equalities) and depends on BSD for the converse. (3) Implicit in (1)-(2): the rank (and the 2-primary Tate-Shafarevich data) of the family E_n. Note: the literal wording says 'rational numbers', while the literature restricts to positive squarefree integers; I treat the problem as the literature does and flag the difference.

events.what_happened: Heegner (1952), as summarised in a lecture-note search snippet (original not opened): rational points constructed on the curves give that n = 2p is congruent for every prime p = 3 mod 4. Heegner's construction was extended by Monsky (1990) and Birch-Stephens for prime cases (see monsky-1990).
events.delivers: Congruence of n = 2p for each prime p = 3 mod 4 (as summarised). A family of congruent numbers, not a characterisation.
events.remains: All other n, including every n with an odd prime factor pattern outside this family; the characterisation as a whole.
events.directly_checkable: Explicit rational right triangles can be checked by hand for small n; the 2p family is a construction on the curve for n.
events.direction: Toward congruence, for the family n = 2p, p = 3 mod 4. Not a counterexample to anything asserted.

events.what_happened: Monsky (1990), as summarised on Wikipedia's Congruent number page (original not opened): for a prime p, p = 3 mod 8 is not congruent but 2p is; p = 5 mod 8 is congruent; p = 7 mod 8 means both p and 2p are congruent. Monsky's method is the 2-Selmer matrix approach, and the Wikipedia page attributes these cases to him.
events.delivers: Congruence or non-congruence for primes p and 2p in the residue classes stated; for composite n, nothing in the summary.
events.remains: Composite n with several odd prime factors; the classes 1, 2, 3 mod 8 beyond the prime cases stated; the characterisation as a whole.
events.directly_checkable: The prime cases are checkable via 2-descent for a given p; I did not verify any case.
events.direction: Both toward congruence (p = 5, 7 mod 8; 2p for p = 3 mod 8 and 7 mod 8) and toward non-congruence (p = 3 mod 8).

events.what_happened: Tunnell's criterion, Inventiones Mathematicae 72(2) (1983), 323-334. For squarefree n, four counts A_n, B_n, C_n, D_n of integer solutions of ternary quadratic forms (for odd n: 2x^2+y^2+32z^2 and 2x^2+y^2+8z^2; for even n: 8x^2+2y^2+64z^2 and 8x^2+2y^2+16z^2, as reported in the secondary sources). Unconditionally: if n is congruent and odd then 2A_n = B_n; if even then 2C_n = D_n. Conversely, if BSD holds for y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x, these equalities imply that n is congruent. The statement was taken from the Wikipedia page and from secondary restatements (arXiv 1504.07507 and Stein/Williamstein notes via search snippets); the 1983 paper itself was not accessible.
events.delivers: A finite, computable test for each squarefree n: necessary unconditionally, sufficient only given BSD for the family. It settles the question for each individual n if BSD holds, and reduces it to counting.
events.remains: An unconditional converse (sufficiency) for all n; so the unconditional determination of which n are congruent.
events.directly_checkable: For a given n, count the solutions of the four ternary forms in a bounded box; this is the criterion used for the computations in trillion-2009.
events.direction: Forward direction: a congruent n must satisfy the count equalities (unconditional). Converse: equalities imply congruence, conditional on BSD. It is the classical baseline the later events are measured against; it cuts neither way on its own.

events.what_happened: A computation resolving the congruence status of all squarefree n up to 10^12 (a trillion), reported in September 2009 by a team from North America, Europe, Australia and South America. Secondary reports give about 3.15 billion congruent numbers up to a trillion (one report gives 3,148,379,694). The computation uses Tunnell's criterion, and its results are stated to depend on BSD for these curves (converse direction); the computation was reportedly run twice on different computers, with different algorithms, written by two independent groups. Sources are press and AIM news pages seen in search snippets; I did not open them.
events.delivers: Congruence status of every squarefree n up to 10^12, conditional on BSD for the converse. Finitely many instances.
events.remains: All n above 10^12; the characterisation as a whole.

A search summary of the paper's statement says infinitely many square-free congruent numbers with k+1 odd prime divisors in each class 5, 6, 7 mod 8 (indexing not checked against the full text).

events.remains: Classes 1, 2, 3 mod 8 (the method gives no congruence there); all n in 5, 6, 7 mod 8 that are not of the constructed shape; the characterisation as a whole.

events.what_happened: Alexander Smith, 'The congruent numbers have positive natural density', arXiv:1603.08479 (v1 28 Mar 2016; v2 29 Mar 2016). Abstract (opened): 'We prove that the rational elliptic curve y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x satisfies the full Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for at least 41.9% of positive squarefree integers n equal to 1, 2, or 3 mod 8, and that it satisfies the regular BSD conjecture for at least 55.9% of positive squarefree integers n equal to 5, 6, or 7 mod 8. In particular, at least 55.9% of positive squarefree integers equal to 5, 6, or 7 mod 8 are congruent numbers. These proofs complete an argument started by Tian, Yuan, and Zhang.' Journal publication not identified in sources I read.
events.delivers: Unconditional per the abstract's 'We prove' wording: positive lower density (at least 55.9%) of congruent numbers among squarefree n = 5, 6, 7 mod 8. Lower bounds on proportions, not densities. For n = 1, 2, 3 mod 8, full BSD for E_n in at least 41.9% of cases, which gives rank 0 information for those n.
events.remains: The remaining proportion of n = 5, 6, 7 mod 8 (at most 44.1% not covered by the bound); the exact density; the 1, 2, 3 mod 8 classes for congruence; the characterisation as a whole.

events.what_happened: Alexander Smith, '2^infinity-Selmer groups, 2^infinity-class groups, and Goldfeld's conjecture', arXiv:1702.02325 (v1 8 Feb 2017; v2 7 Jun 2017; 84 pages). events.what_happened: Frank Vega, 'Sharp-P and the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture', EasyChair Preprint 9368 (26 Nov 2022; the page opened shows v2 and links a v3). Conditional on BSD: for odd square-free n, congruence is equivalent to a count of solutions of one ternary form being twice that of another (Tunnell). Claims: the counting problem is an instance of a #P-complete problem (no proof on the page); deciding congruence is in NP because a congruum is a certificate; conjecture that if P = NP and FP != #P then BSD would be false. A search snippet says v3 presents the last conjecture as a formal conclusion with a proof section (not verified).
events.revisions: EasyChair page shows v2 (26 Nov 2022); v3 linked as current (date not recorded).
events.delivers: Conditional on BSD: a complexity-theoretic reframing of Tunnell's counting criterion. Does not change the set of congruent numbers or decide any n unconditionally.
events.remains: The whole characterisation; the #P-completeness claim is asserted and not proved on the page read.
events.doubts: (1) The #P-completeness claim is asserted without proof on the page. (2) The NP claim depends on the congruum certificate, stated without a full argument on the page. (3) The main link is conditional on BSD. (4) EasyChair preprints are not peer-reviewed, as the platform itself says.
events.direction: Conditional and complexity-theoretic: under P = NP and FP != #P, BSD would be false (conjecture). Does not move the problem as stated.

events.what_happened: Heng Chen, Rong Ma, Tuoping Du, 'An exact way to verify whether n is a congruent number using Heegner points', arXiv:2411.14188 (v1, 21 Nov 2024). The page also carries a 'Date: August 24, 2026' line that conflicts with the arXiv stamp. Content (opened): computes the conductor of y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x (asserted as 2^5 n^2 for all n); Theorem 6.1: with U the sum of Heegner-point images under the modular parametrisation, if U is not in the torsion-type set S_n then n is congruent; uses Gross-Zagier (Prop. 6.1), Silverman and Knapp (Theorem 6.2). Worked examples: n = 5 (explicit point) and n = 13 (numerical test, Theorem 7.1: '13 is a congruent number').

(3) The Goldfeld-conjecture statement on the page is garbled. (4) Full conditions of the test were not readable in the text I accessed; the paper does not say whether the method depends on BSD, and I did not establish that.

events.what_happened: Neither manuscript mentions congruent numbers or Tunnell's theorem. The link runs through E₀: y² = x³ − x. Its twist by a squarefree d is E₀^(d): d·y² = x³ − x, which over Q is y² = x³ − d²x (substitute X = dx, Y = d²y). For n > 0 squarefree this is the congruent-number curve E_n: y² = x³ − n²x. Both manuscripts apply to E₀ as they apply to any E/Q. The Goldfeld-density manuscript (Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026) gives the 2-converse and the density theorem described under the BSD entry. The mean-rank manuscript (The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-October-6-2026) gives mean analytic rank 1/2 over signed squarefree twists of E₀. The following is my derivation from those theorems. It is not stated in either manuscript. (i) Because E₀^(n) and E₀^(−n) are the same curve, the signed counts split evenly between positive and negative n, so the density statements hold over positive squarefree n with the same values: analytic rank 0 and analytic rank 1 each have density 1/2, and c₂ ∈ {0,1} has density one. (ii) For positive squarefree n with c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1}, the 2-converse gives ord_{s=1}L(E_n,s) = rank E_n(Q) = c₂(E_n). Since n is congruent exactly when E_n(Q) has positive rank (the standard equivalence for squarefree n, where E_n(Q) has torsion (Z/2)²), we get: n is congruent ⇔ c₂(E_n) = 1 ⇔ L(E_n,1) = 0. No BSD assumption is used. The classical Tunnell route needs BSD for the step 'L(E_n,1) = 0 implies n congruent'; for n with c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1} this manuscript supplies that step unconditionally. (iii) The set of n with c₂(E_n) ≥ 2 has density zero, since Smith's count, which the Goldfeld manuscript uses, makes c₂ ∈ {0,1} density one. Together with (i) and (ii), this gives that congruent numbers have asymptotic density 1/2 among positive squarefree integers.
events.revisions: 2 earlier edition(s) kept in the repository: Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-September-23-2026, The-mean-analytic-rank-of-quadratic-twists-of-elliptic-curves-September-23-2026
events.delivers: Restricted to positive squarefree n with c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1}, the family decides congruence unconditionally, with 'congruent' equal to 'L(E_n,1) = 0' and to '2-Selmer corank 1' (step ii above). The family's own statements give density 1/2 for analytic rank 0 and for analytic rank 1 among the twists of E₀, and by (i) and (iii), density 1/2 for congruent numbers among positive squarefree integers. These are asymptotic statements. They do not say whether any particular n is congruent, and they do not give a procedure that decides every n. The problem asks to 'determine precisely what rational numbers are congruent numbers'. This family does not meet that demand, which needs a criterion for every n.
events.remains: (a) A criterion that decides every n. For n with c₂(E_n) ≥ 2 nothing is said, and the family gives no computation of c₂(E_n) for any particular n. (b) The density-zero exceptional set where c₂(E_n) ≥ 2 is not resolved. (c) Tunnell's L-value criterion is neither stated nor proved in these manuscripts, so the problem's named route is not reproduced here. (d) Non-integral rationals: the manuscripts say nothing about them. The reduction to positive squarefree integers is the literature's convention, and the problem's literal 'rational numbers' wording is not addressed.
events.doubts: (1) No manuscript mentions congruent numbers, Tunnell's theorem, or the density of congruent numbers. Steps (i) to (iii) are my derivation from the stated theorems and should be weighed as such. (2) The density theorems are stated for the signed count. The reduction to positive n uses E₀^(n) = E₀^(−n), which I checked from the twist formula; the manuscripts do not state it. (3) The Goldfeld manuscript's introduction cites congruent-number literature (Tian; Smith; Kriz; and BurungaleTian2026, Theorem 1.2, which gives rank zero for almost all positive squarefree n ≡ 1, 2, 3 mod 8 in the family n·y² = x³ − x). These are cited as background, and the family does not rely on them. (4) The density statements are asymptotic, and nothing in the text says which n are congruent.; conditional on: Step (ii) uses the 2-converse for E_n, which applies only where c₂(E_n) ∈ {0,1}; the manuscripts give no way to check that for a given n. The density statements use Smith2025 Theorem 1.1 (external, not reproved here). The facts 'congruent ⇔ positive rank for squarefree n' and 'E_n(Q) has torsion (Z/2)²' are standard results used from outside the family. The rest of the dependencies are as in the BSD entry: Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin, Kato, Waldspurger, Howard, Monsky and Cassels.

Prastaro (2015) claims unconditional sufficiency of Tunnell's criterion, which would solve the problem. The Tunnell discussion in the same paper, as quoted in a search snippet, states the converse conditionally on BSD. No acceptance, refutation or citing work found.

The OpenAI BSD manuscripts carry different titles and dates across sources: 'Exact Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank' (repository history entry 7 Oct 2026) and 'The two-primary Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one' (Sept 2026, per a GitHub issue and catalogue), with VibeMathed giving 24 Sep 2026. summary: Searched 48 queries and opened about 40 pages, some of them blocked (see incomplete). Status: the problem as stated is still open. No event since 26 January 2024 gives an unconditional characterisation of the congruent numbers, and Wikipedia's status line ('as of 2019, this problem has not been brought to a successful resolution') is still accurate in that sense. In-window congruent-number work is partial or conditional: (i) explicit infinite families of non-congruent n in classes 1, 2, 3 mod 8 (Das-Mondal, 29 Apr 2026), which may overlap with Smith's 2017 result (100% of those n non-congruent, a secondary attribution I could not confirm in the full text); (ii) necessary conditions via class numbers (Das-Mondal 25 Apr 2026, listed in Journal of Algebra; Das-De-Mondal 26 Apr 2026); (iii) a per-n Heegner-point test (Chen-Ma-Du, 21 Nov 2024), whose only worked examples are n = 5 and n = 13, both already known to be congruent; (iv) rank-zero statements for density sets: Burungale-Tian (4 Jun 2025, CM p-converse, about 50% of square-free n for the twists n y^2 = x^3 - x, exact class not readable, Annals acceptance stated but not confirmed) and Xu (3 Sep 2026, n = 17q and 34q for a density-5/128 set of primes q, conditional status not stated). Variants (theta-congruent, pi/3) and a data-science study (Deshpande et al.) are recorded and discounted. The largest in-window item is OpenAI's September-October 2026 BSD manuscripts, released with 722 manuscripts on 6 Oct 2026. Claimed: rank equals Selmer corank for E/Q with corank 0 or 1 at some prime; a pointwise 2-converse for curves with rational 2-torsion (every congruent-number curve y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x has full 2-torsion); and a Goldfeld density claim. If correct, these would decide congruence for every n whose 2-Selmer corank of E_n is 0 or 1, a subset I cannot size. I could not read the manuscripts (their PDFs are binary to WebFetch), so the claim that they reach y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x is my inference from the general scope statements in secondary sources, not from the text. AI attribution: the repository README states 'The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model' and gives an average of three hours of ChatGPT Pro-equivalent compute per result, with about 4,000 problems posed; no model name is given, and the BSD entries are not named individually. Verification: VibeMathed lists the BSD and 2-converse results as 'Unreviewed'; a commentator's first impression calls the BSD results 'technical improvements on results already in the literature' and 'no genuine progress towards the higher-rank version of BSD'; the Goldfeld companion has an open GitHub dispute on congruent-number numerics. Withdrawals: the three retracted manuscripts (7 Oct 2026) concern the Hodge conjecture, not BSD, per the sources I read. Unverified BSD proofs: Matnyak (2014, not opened), Lippy (June 2025; headings only), an 'Iran formula' preprint (May 2025; index title only), and a Medium post 'Bridge of Creation' (undated, blocked; not recorded as an event). Prastaro (April 2015) is the one pre-window unconditional claim: its abstract has no conditional hypothesis, yet the Tunnell discussion (as quoted in a snippet) is conditional; nothing accepts or refutes it in the sources I found. Other AI-related work in this area: rank records for general curves credited to Claude (unreleased version), Aug 2026, not identified as congruent-number curves; an AI-assisted paper on tilings by congruent triangles, which is a different problem. competing_reading: Read the OpenAI BSD-family claims as substantial: if the rank-equals-corank statement is right and applies to E_n, it settles congruence for every n whose 2-Selmer (or any q-Selmer) corank is 0 or 1, and combined with Smith (2016: at least 55.9% of n = 5, 6, 7 mod 8 congruent, unconditionally per its abstract) and Burungale-Tian (about 50% of square-free n with analytic rank 0), a large share of the family could be determined. Opposite reading: none of the in-window results decides any n whose Selmer corank is at least 2, the density results are lower bounds, the OpenAI claims are unreviewed with an open dispute on the companion manuscript, and the problem's 'precisely' remains unmet for the bulk of the family. A third reading: Smith (2017) and the new explicit families of Das-Mondal overlap in the classes 1, 2, 3 mod 8, so their in-window contribution there may be explicitness rather than new decisions.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The text of the OpenAI manuscripts 'A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion' (paper.pdf) and 'Exact Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank' in github.com/openai/math: whether they state the result for y^2 = x^3 - n^2 x (or n y^2 = x^3 - x) and what they prove for corank 0 and 1 at 2. (b) Specialist referee reports on those manuscripts, and on the disputed mod-8 step in the Goldfeld companion (GitHub issue borism/openai-math-slop#1), with a resolution of whether the branch is empty. (c) Lean formalisation status for each of these entries. (d) For Prastaro (2015): a journal acceptance or a published refutation of the bordism argument, or a statement from the author on the conditional/unconditional question. (e) For Smith (2017): the full text of arXiv 1702.02325, to confirm the 100% non-congruence statement for n = 1, 2, 3 mod 8. (f) For Burungale-Tian: the exact display for the 50% statement and the class of n it covers, and the Annals publication record. (g) For Xu (2026): whether the rank-zero result for E_{17q} and E_{34q} is conditional, and whether it is refereed. (h) For Chen-Ma-Du: a general theorem with a range of n beyond 5 and 13, and a statement of whether the method depends on BSD.

judgement.why: The statement asks for a precise determination of every congruent number, so any result deciding a family of n (Heegner, Monsky, Tian, TYZ, Das-Mondal, Xu, the OpenAI low-Selmer-corank converse) is a case, while proportion results (Smith 2016/2017, Burungale-Tian 50%) are bounds. Tunnell's unconditional forward direction decides non-congruence wherever the counts differ, so it is a case rather than a mere reduction. Whole-problem BSD proof claims (Matnyak, Prastaro, Iran formula, Lippy) carry several F10 signals together and are set aside. Chen-Ma-Du decides only already-known n and is none; the trillion computation and Deshpande are instances; theta- and pi/3-congruent and rank records are variants. The OpenAI rows are scored generated from the README's statement that results were obtained by the internal model; the record shows no human mathematical authorship. Close calls: Burungale-Tian and Das-Mondal 8k+3 marked digested on stated journal acceptance (Annals, J. Algebra) not independently confirmed; OpenAI events doubtful rather than knocked down because the GitHub issue's author themselves says it is not a disproof.
judgement.doubts: openai-bsd-2026 and openai-math-002 describe the same family (002), and openai-2-converse-2026 / openai-goldfeld-2026 overlap openai-math-006; they are scored separately but are not independent results. The OpenAI AI attribution rests on a general README sentence not naming these manuscripts. The congruent-number consequence of the OpenAI theorems is the researcher's deduction. Smith 2016 'digested' could be argued from Goldfeld's prize write-up, but that was a snippet only.
